role_summary: Senior backend engineer for Helio Labs's payments infrastructure team. The role owns the next generation of the ledger and payment-rails service: high-throughput transactional systems where correctness is load-bearing and failure modes need to be reasoned about end-to-end. The hire will be one of the first three ICs on the team, partnering with a staff engineer on the architectural direction.
minimum_bar_description: Six years of backend engineering, with at least three years on systems where correctness under concurrent load was a primary design constraint. Candidates whose entire experience has been in CRUD-heavy product surfaces with no exposure to ledger, queue, or concurrency-heavy work will read as a stretch.

capability_areas.name: Distributed systems at scale
capability_areas.description: Has owned a service that handles meaningful production traffic and made the architectural calls that shape how it scales. The candidate should have a recruiter-readable answer to "what was the hardest distributed-systems problem you had to solve, and how did you think about it."
builder_signals: Tenure on a system with measurable scale — RPS, transaction volume, or geographic distribution that forced real architectural choices.
Job titles or scope language that names the system: "ledger service," "payments core," "event router," rather than generic "backend engineer."
Trajectory shows depth in one substrate over years rather than a sequence of one-year company-hops with shallow surface area at each.
user_signals: "Built REST APIs at scale" with no scale referenced anywhere; the word scale is doing all the work.
Resume reads as full-stack with backend as one of five things; backend depth is not the spine.
Architectural calls described in passive voice ("the system was designed to") suggesting the candidate consumed decisions rather than made them.

capability_areas.name: Payment systems integrations
capability_areas.description: Has shipped or maintained code that talks to a real payment processor, banking partner, or settlement system. Knows what idempotency means in practice — not as a CS-101 concept but as the set of bugs you debug at 2am.
builder_signals: Named integration work — Stripe, Adyen, Plaid, Modern Treasury, or in-house equivalents at fintechs of comparable stage.
Evidence of having reasoned about the operational surface: webhooks, retries, settlement reconciliation, dispute handling.
Has held a production rotation on payments-adjacent code; knows the failure modes from the inside.
user_signals: Payments listed as a tag among twenty other tags with no project depth visible.
Resume asserts "integrated Stripe" but doesn't name a single design decision that was non-obvious.
Tenure at a fintech but on the consumer surface (mobile app, growth) rather than the rails.

capability_areas.name: Production infra ownership
capability_areas.description: Has carried the pager for systems they wrote. The brief is not looking for a pure architect — the strongest candidates have been on call, written the runbook, and made the call to roll back at 3am.
builder_signals: Explicit on-call language; specific war-story-worthy incidents the candidate names in their writing.
Has chosen and defended infra primitives — Kafka vs RabbitMQ, Postgres vs Spanner — on a real project, with written evidence of the reasoning.
Trajectory toward staff-track or principal scope at their current company, suggesting depth was rewarded.
user_signals: "Worked closely with infra" framing — adjacent to the work rather than owning it.
Pure platform-engineering role with no evidence of having written application code that used the infra they built.
Recent move into engineering management with the IC depth visible only several years back.

depth_distinction.builder_definition: The builder has authored a meaningful piece of the substrate that processes money. They can speak in specifics about a deadlock they debugged, a write-amplification failure they engineered around, or a settlement-reconciliation bug that taught them something they now believe. They read other people's distributed-systems code with the eye of someone who has paid the cost of getting it wrong.
depth_distinction.user_definition: The user has used the substrate without owning it. Their role was to plug into a payments service that someone else built and call its endpoints from a feature surface. They can describe what the system did from the outside, but the questions about why it was shaped that way fall to the staff engineer two seats over.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: Borderline cases are usually candidates with two years at a payments company on the right team but coming off a four-year stretch on the wrong substrate before that. The signal to watch is whether the recent depth is convincing on its own — if the work-products from those two years would let them lead the next greenfield service here, lean save. If their best stories still come from the prior chapter, they are user-tier.

non_fit_patterns.label: Consultancy track with late fintech pivot
non_fit_patterns.description: Pure consultancy track for the first half of the resume; payment-systems work appears only in the last 18 months.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The substrate exposure is too thin to lead the next greenfield service. The candidate would need a staff-level partner to compensate for the missing years.

non_fit_patterns.label: Crypto-only fintech depth
non_fit_patterns.description: Heavy crypto / web3 background with no traditional-rails fintech depth; the substrate vocabulary is different and the brief is not for a crypto rebuild.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Settlement, banking-partner integration, and reconciliation are different problems than on-chain finality. The transferable depth is real but not what this role is buying.

non_fit_patterns.label: Manager-only recency
non_fit_patterns.description: Manager-only for the past three years; IC chops have not been kept current.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role is IC; a candidate whose recent contributions are coaching and roadmaps will be slow to be load-bearing on the substrate.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Confirmed tenure on a payments-rails or ledger team, not the consumer-product surface.
The role and team matter more than the logo; depth varies wildly inside these orgs.
Payments-team tenure required to count as direct depth; otherwise treat as general-systems prior.

minimum_bar: Six years total backend experience; three years on transactional / payment-adjacent / ledger systems; demonstrable IC ownership of a service handling meaningful production load.
